inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K via SEC XBRL: ShareBasedCompensation 120 (cash-flow add-back) + AdjustmentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 37 (taxes on net-share settlement; no combined figure published). H1-2026 SBC already 107, so forward path is set at 0.45% of revenue, above the FY2025 0.39%.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 weighted diluted shares (293.9m, 10-Q). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. CBRE is a heavy repurchaser (FY2025 $968m, H1-2026 $940m), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Corporate debt at 2026-06-30: long-term debt 5,731 + current maturities 69 + short-term borrowings ex-warehouse ~1,575 (ShortTermBorrowings 2,293 less warehouse lines 711 less other 7; commercial paper/revolver drawn to fund Pearce and buybacks) + finance-lease liabilities 229 = 7,604; less cash 1,489. Warehouse lines (711) excluded: they are self-liquidating funding of mortgage loans held for sale (Advisory loan servicing), matched by those loans.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.15 -> cost of equity ~10.0%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.0% on ~16% debt weight -> ~9.0%. Single WACC across scenarios: cyclicality is charged through the bear path and weights, not a premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease cost (FY2025 $319m) sits inside operating expenses, so EBITDA is already post-rent and operating-lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. Finance leases (liability $229m) are in net debt because their principal payments sit in financing, outside FCF. One treatment each, never both.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (incl. 40% outside stake in Turner & Townsend and other partly-owned subs). NCI charged once in the equity bridge at ~12x FY2025 NCI earnings (120 NCI + 26 redeemable NCI = 146) = -1,750, versus book 776 (322 NCI + 454 redeemable NCI).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon. CBRE is a fee-earning commercial real estate SERVICES operating company (advisory/brokerage, facilities and project management, investment management) -- it does not own an IAS-40 property portfolio or distribute AFFO, so the REIT row does not apply; the cyclical-operating-company row of dcf-methods routes it to owner-FCF. Base EBITDA is GAAP operating income + D&A (FY2025 2,482 = 6.1%) plus SBC (120) = 6.4% pre-SBC, NOT management's Core EBITDA, which also adds back integration/carried-interest items. D&A (1.8% of revenue) is inflated by acquired-intangible amortization (393 in FY2025, scheduled 376/322/292/260/236) and is glided down toward ~1.1% as it rolls off. Acquisitions (FY2025 $1.37bn cash, incl. Pearce $1.2bn Nov-25) are NOT modelled: revenue growth paths are meant to be mostly organic plus the already-paid-for Pearce/Industrious contribution; a CBRE that keeps buying growth will out-grow these paths but at the cost of cash the model does not charge. Interest income not stripped (net debt company). Cash tax on unlevered EBIT ~23% (FY2025 GAAP ETR 19.9% on levered pretax; cash taxes 599). FY2025 equity-award taxes (37) backfilled to kpis via make fix. Q2-2026 10-Q is the latest filing; Q3 2026 results due late October.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests incl. redeemable NCI (~12x FY2025 NCI earnings of 146)
Equity-method investments (co-investments in funds and development JVs) at book
equity_bridge.note: XBRL EquityMethodInvestments 2026-06-30; their income (equity income, FY2025 40) sits below operating income and is excluded from the flows

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr, trimmed for acquired growth. Equity CAGR rejected: $4.1bn of buybacks FY2021-25 shrank book value, so it does not measure business growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.2% vs revenue 11.2% / EPS 11.6% (>30% divergence) -- caused by buybacks, not by the business. Owner-FCF CAGRs are negative because FY2020-21 were peak cash years (2020 deferred taxes/comp, 2021 transaction boom) and FY2023 owner FCF was ~0 on a working-capital/bonus unwind; the endpoints, not the trend, drive those figures.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes): FY2020 1,460; FY2021 1,930; FY2022 1,171; FY2023 7; FY2024 1,150; FY2025 1,036. Reported FCF is levered (interest paid 448 in FY2025) -- the forward build is unlevered, so year-1 owner FCF (~1.8bn) sits above the FY2025 levered figure by roughly after-tax interest plus FY2026 growth. SBC-adjusted CAGR sits slightly above reported (SBC has not outgrown cash flow).

base.narrative: FY2026 at guidance (H1 revenue +17%, core EPS $7.80-7.90 raised; Q4 flat), FY2027 at the >=15% core-EPS guide on ~9% revenue, then glide to 3.5% as the transaction recovery matures and data-centre services slow from ~25% to mid-teens. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 6.6% -> 7.3% on mix shift to infrastructure/BOE and operating leverage in Advisory.

scenario_narratives.base: The resilient ~65% (facilities/BOE, Project Management via Turner & Townsend, Pearce and data-centre technical services) compounds high-single digits while leasing and capital markets complete a normal recovery from the 2023-24 trough. FY2026 lands at the raised core-EPS guide and FY2027 at the >=15% initial guide; thereafter growth fades to ~3.5% as data-centre services decelerate from ~25% toward mid-teens and the transaction cycle matures. Margins expand modestly (6.6% -> 7.3% pre-SBC EBITDA on gross revenue) from infrastructure mix and Advisory operating leverage, capped because the BOE/Project Management revenue carries thin pass-through margins.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI data-centre build-out runs at management's ~25%/yr through 2030 and the $10bn infrastructure revenue / $1bn+ EBITDA target is hit; leasing and capital-markets volumes return to 2021-22 levels as rates settle; Investment Management fundraising reopens. Revenue compounds ~10% for five years and pre-SBC EBITDA margin reaches 8.0% as higher-margin Advisory and infrastructure services mix up. Exit at 17x owner FCF, in line with a less-cyclical outsourcing compounder.
scenario_narratives.bear: A renewed CRE downturn or higher-for-longer rates hits in 2027-28: capital-markets and leasing fees fall 30-40% as in 2023, Investment Management fundraising stays shut, and an AI-capex pause or power/permitting bottlenecks stall data-centre services. Revenue flat then -4%, pre-SBC margin compresses to 5.3% (Advisory operating deleverage on a people-heavy cost base), with the M&A-funded leverage (corporate debt ~$7.6bn, up from ~$3.3bn at FY2024) limiting buybacks. Recovery to only 6.2% margins and 3% growth; 12x exit reflects a market that re-rates CBRE as a cyclical broker.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): roughly a third of revenue is transactional and rate-sensitive, the cycle has already recovered sharply, and leverage has doubled to fund M&A and buybacks -- but the resilient majority and no refinancing stress keep it well short of distress weights. Base 50%: guidance was just raised and FY2027 guided. Bull 30% (below 35%): it needs both the data-centre target and a full transaction recovery to land together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CBRE valued as a cyclical fee-based services operating company on unlevered owner FCF with SBC and equity-award taxes fully expensed and the share count held flat (buybacks fund it). Components are built from GAAP operating income + D&A rather than management's Core EBITDA; acquired-intangible amortization rolls off; acquisitions are not modelled, so growth paths are organic plus already-paid deals. Cyclicality is charged once, through a genuine downturn bear path and a 20% bear weight, not through a WACC premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: Transaction cycle: leasing and capital-markets fees are the swing factor; a 2023-style drop compresses margin by ~1.3pp
Data-centre services growth (~25%/yr guided) is the main source of above-GDP growth; an AI-capex pause removes it
Acquisition-driven growth: the model does not charge future M&A spend, and does not credit M&A-driven revenue either
Short-term borrowings split (commercial paper/revolver vs warehouse lines) is inferred from XBRL; a ~$0.5bn error moves value ~$1.7/share
NCI valued at ~12x earnings; Turner & Townsend buy-out terms could differ
